html:
The Paiter, also called Suruí, are an Indigenous people of Rondônia in western Brazil, near the border with Mato Grosso. They speak a Mondé language of the Tupian family.

They had their first peaceful contact with Brazilian government agents in 1969, as roads and settlers pushed into the region. Epidemics followed and killed most of them within a few years. Their reserve, Sete de Setembro, was later invaded by loggers and miners. Under their leader Almir Narayamoga Suruí they became known for defending it with modern tools: a partnership with Google to map the forest, and a forest carbon project. Their neighbours include the Cinta Larga and the Karitiana.
